prompt_text:
Analyze the following vulnerability patch and generate a precise Semgrep rule specification (as a JSON object) to detect similar vulnerabilities in typescript code. CONTEXT: Repository: github.com/streetwriters/notesnook Commit: e87f5e5f899f45df28d7c0f33f15e9178d1fbcb7 PATCH CHANGES: File: packages/editor/src/extensions/embed/component.tsx --- a/packages/editor/src/extensions/embed/component.tsx +++ b/packages/editor/src/extensions/embed/component.tsx + + const anchor = document.createElement("a"); + anchor.href = `${src}?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw`; + - }>

`; + }>

${ + anchor.outerHTML + }

`; JSON FIELDS (emit a single JSON object with exactly these field names): - "id": "vuln-notesnook-e87f5e5f" (must be unique and descriptive, lowercase letters/digits/hyphens only) - "message": detailed description of what the vulnerability is, why it's dangerous, and how to fix it - "severity": one of "ERROR", "WARNING", "INFO" - "languages": ["typescript"] - "metadata": an object, e.g. {"category": "security", "cwe": "...", "owasp": "..."} - exactly ONE of: "pattern": a single pattern string matching the vulnerable code structure, using $VARNAME for any expression and ... for any sequence of statements "pattern_either": a list of alternative pattern strings (any of which should match) "taint_sources" + "taint_sinks": each a list of pattern strings (taint-tracking mode) - optionally also: "pattern_not": a list of one or more pattern strings that should NOT match (e.g. the fixed version) -- you do not need to know how this combines with "pattern"; that is handled for you "pattern_inside": a single pattern string restricting matches to inside this context "pattern_not_inside": a single pattern string excluding matches inside this context IMPORTANT GUIDELINES: 1. Make "pattern" (or "pattern_either") as specific as possible to minimize false positives 2. Include "pattern_not" for the fixed version when possible 3. Add relevant metadata like CWE numbers and OWASP categories 4. Write a clear, actionable "message" explaining both the problem and the fix 5. Consider different variations of the vulnerable pattern EXAMPLES OF HIGH-QUALITY RULE SPECIFICATIONS: Respond with ONLY the JSON object, nothing else.

messages.content:
You generate Semgrep rule specifications as a single JSON object.
    Return ONLY the raw JSON object -- no markdown fences, no YAML, no explanatory text before or after it.
    Do not compose Semgrep operators (patterns:, pattern-either:, etc.) yourself -- a separate deterministic
    serializer does that from the plain fields you provide. Supported fields: id, message, severity,
    languages, metadata (all required except metadata), plus exactly ONE of: pattern (a single pattern
    string), pattern_either (a list of alternative pattern strings), or taint_sources + taint_sinks
    (each a list of pattern strings, used together). Optionally also: pattern_not (a list of one or more
    exclusion pattern strings), pattern_inside (a single scope-restriction pattern string),
    pattern_not_inside (a single negative-scope pattern string). taint rules cannot combine with
    pattern_not/pattern_inside/pattern_not_inside.
